meaning: something that is very easy to do
example: The test was a piece of cake.
origin: The exact origin is unclear; it may come from the idea that eating cake is easy

wrong_meanings.why_wrong: This is the literal meaning of the words, not the idiomatic one
The idiom has nothing to do with price or gifts

wrong_meanings.meaning: a plan that is sure to fail
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: The idiom describes something easy, not something that will go wrong

explanation: 'Piece of cake' means that something is very easy to do. People use it to say that a task did not cause any problems.
